value.body: A two-year master's in the business of tourism — tour operations, travel agency management, destination planning, hospitality, tourism marketing and policy. Universities offer it as an MTTM (Master of Tourism and Travel Management) or an MBA in tourism; the Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM), under the Ministry of Tourism, also runs an MBA in this area.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Usually includes an internship with a travel or hospitality firm

items.label: PG students in tourism management
items.note: All PG programmes reported under this subject
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, PG enrolment by subject, actual responses (Ministry of Education)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree in any subject, usually with a minimum percentage. Admission is through a university entrance test, CUET-PG at participating universities, or a management test (such as CAT, MAT or CMAT) accepted by the institute, followed by a group discussion or interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: It suits those aiming for travel-company, tour-operations or tourism-board roles at a higher entry level.
Placements depend heavily on the tourism cycle and the institute's industry links.
A UGC-NET in tourism administration and management can lead to college teaching.
